Each one-year increase in patient age is associated with a **change in log-odds of remission of −0.0795** (per year), i.e., β_Age = −0.079508, from the specified logistic regression `remission ∼ Age + BMI + Gender` (Male=1, Female=0 reference) fitted on the n = 80 complete-case patients. Equivalently, older age lowers remission odds: OR = exp(β_Age) = 0.924 per additional year (≈ 7.6% lower odds per year), holding BMI and gender constant. Supporting statistics for β_Age: SE = 0.026298, 95% CI [−0.131051, −0.027966], p = 0.0025.

In full: each additional year of age decreases the log-odds of remission by **0.0795 (95% CI −0.131 to −0.028, p = 0.002)**, adjusted for BMI and gender, on the raw per-year age scale.
